abstract.para: Go is an open source, statically typed, compiled programming language designed for building reliable and efficient software.

section.title: Lifecycle and support policy
section.para: On &suselinux; 16, Go and its components are updated and supported according to the following rules:

listitem.para: In sync with upstream, which nominally releases every six months, in February and August. Updates are integrated within a two-month sliding window following each upstream release.
Versions N and N-1, mirroring the upstream support policy. When a new major version is released, the oldest supported version enters a two-month sliding grace period for transition before retirement.
Go minor releases are made available shortly after the upstream release.
Supported. Versions are parallel installable and undergo automated testing. The go metapackage always points to the latest go1.x package.
General Support and LTS for all relevant &suselinux; minor releases

section.title: Building Go applications
section.para: When building applications, developers have the following options regarding versions:

listitem.para: Depend on a minimum version, for example, BuildRequires: golang(API) >= go1.23.
Pin a specific go1.x package, for example, BuildRequires: golang(API) == go1.23.
In both cases, use the go1.x version given in the go directive of the application's go.mod file, because the Go compiler now requires it as a minimum version.

section.title: FIPS compliance
section.para: Alongside standard go1.xx releases, &suse; provides a parallel go1.xx-openssl variant. This version is specifically patched to use OpenSSL for FIPS-compliant cryptographic operations.

Starting with go1.24, Go upstream introduced an integrated FIPS 140-3 cryptographic implementation. As this implementation achieves certification, the parallel go1.xx-openssl variant will be deprecated in favor of the upstream-supported FIPS mechanism. &suse; packaging follows the upstream deprecation schedule and support lifecycle.
